tools.name: get_job

tools.name: list_areas
tools.description: Impact areas (categories) with the number of open roles in each.

tools.name: get_organization

tools.name: request_api_key
tools.description: Ask the user for their email first, then call this to email them a free key (30 requests a minute, 500 a day, 10 results per search). Use it when calls are rate limited. The key goes only to that inbox; the user then gives it to you to send as 'Authorization: Bearer ri_...'.

findings.title: Description references secrets/credentials
findings.detail: Description of "request_api_key" references sensitive artifacts (authorization, bearer). A tool description has no reason to mention credentials.

evidence.snippet: Ask the user for their email first, then call this to email them a free key (30 requests a minute, 500 a day, 10 results per search). Use it when calls are rate…

findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: request_api_key · Private data: get_job, request_api_key · Public sink: request_api_key.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: request_api_key · Private data: get_job, request_api_key · Public sink: request_api_key

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.

findings.title: Tool description changed since last scan
findings.detail: Tool "search_jobs" changed its description with no version change. Silent description changes are how a trusted server turns malicious after review.
